Define: Osmosis
items.a: A special form of diffusion where fluid flows from a lower solute concentration, often involving the movement of water into or out of the cell across a selectively permeable membrane.
items.aa: شكل خاص من الانتشار يتدفق فيه السائل من تركيز مذاب أقل، وغالباً يتضمن حركة الماء إلى داخل أو خارج الخلية عبر غشاء نفاذ اختيارياً.

items.q: Define: Phagocytosis
items.a: Cell eating; a specialized type of endocytosis that involves the intake of solid material, food particles, or pathogens into the cell.
items.aa: أكل الخلية؛ نوع متخصص من الإدخال الخلوي يتضمن ابتلاع مواد صلبة، أو جزيئات طعام، أو مسببات الأمراض إلى داخل الخلية.

items.q: Define: Pinocytosis
items.a: Cell drinking; a type of endocytosis that involves the intake of extracellular molecules dissolved in fluid.
items.aa: شرب الخلية؛ نوع من الإدخال الخلوي يتضمن امتصاص الجزيئات خارج الخلية المذابة في السوائل.

items.q: Define: Facilitated Diffusion
items.a: A passive transport process where specific transport protein channels help molecules or ions enter or leave the cell without consuming cellular energy.
items.aa: عملية نقل سلبي تساعد فيها قنوات بروتينية ناقلة محددة الجزيئات أو الأيونات على دخول أو خروج الخلية دون استهلاك طاقة خلوية.

items.q: Define: Active Transport
items.a: Molecular movement across the cell membrane that requires chemical energy (ATP) because it transports substances against their concentration gradient.
items.aa: حركة جزيئية عبر غشاء الخلية تتطلب طاقة كيميائية (ATP) لأنها تنقل المواد عكس تدرج التركيز الخاص بها.

items.q: Define: Exocytosis
items.a: The cellular process by which material is discharged as secretory vesicles move to the cell surface, fuse with the plasma membrane, and expel their contents.
items.aa: العملية الخلوية التي يتم من خلالها إفراز المواد عندما تتحرك الحويصلات الإفرازية نحو سطح الخلية، وتندمج مع الغشاء البلازمي، وتطرد محتوياتها.

handouts.title: Physiology of Body Fluids · فسيولوجيا سوائل الجسم

items.q: Define: Body fluids.
items.a: Liquids originating from inside the bodies of living humans. They include fluids that are excreted or secreted from the body.

items.q: Define: Intracellular fluid (ICF).
items.a: The body fluid located within the cell or all cells of an organism, in the cytoplasm of the cell.

items.q: Define: Extracellular fluid (ECF).
items.a: The body fluid located outside the cell or cells of an organism.

items.q: Define: Interstitial fluid.
items.a: Also known as intercellular fluid and tissue fluid. It is the fluid between the cells of multi-cellular organisms, which delivers materials to the cells, serves intercellular communication, and removes metabolic waste.

items.q: Define: Osmotic pressure.
items.a: The force created by the fluid. Part of it is the oncotic pressure, and it is also called the colloidal osmotic pressure. It pulls the fluid back into the capillary.

items.q: Define: Hydrostatic pressure.
items.a: The force that drives fluid transport (e.g., capillary hydrostatic pressure, CHP: the hydrostatic pressure that blood exerts against the capillary wall). It pushes the fluid out of the capillary.

items.q: Define: Edema.
items.a: A condition in which fluid accumulates in the interstitial compartment. Sometimes it is due to blockage of lymphatic vessels, a lack of plasma proteins, or sodium retention.

items.q: Define: Dehydration.
items.a: A reduced body fluid amount. It can result from reduced water intake or conditions like diarrhea, vomiting, poor fluid intake, bleeding, and increased urine production and sweat.

items.q: Name the two compartments into which body fluid is divided.
Enumerate the components of the extracellular fluid.
List the functions of body fluids.
a: Transportation: delivering oxygen and nutrients throughout the body and removing waste from it.
Digestion: water is an important component of saliva, intestinal and gastric juice.
Maintaining an efficient metabolism of the body.
Lubrication: moistening of tissues and lubricating different joints.

items.q: Besides water, name the groups of molecules that compose body fluid, with examples.
a: Metabolites: urea, glucose, carbon dioxide, oxygen.
Proteins: albumin, hormones, amino acids, antibodies.

items.q: Name the barriers that separate ICF, interstitial fluid and plasma.
a: Plasma membrane: separates ICF from the surrounding interstitial fluid.
Blood vessel wall: separates interstitial fluid from plasma.

items.q: Mention the factors by which the body fluid composition of tissue varies.
a: Tissue type: lean tissues have higher fluid content than fat tissues.
Gender: males have more lean tissue and therefore more body fluid.
Age: lean tissue is lost with age and body fluid is lost with it.

items.q: Which two pressures control the redistribution of water between the body compartments?
What does the interstitial fluid contain?
Mention the common causes of dehydration.
Mention the causes of edema.
Give examples of edema in different parts of the body.
a: Edema (swelling) of the ankles and feet

items.q: State the percentage of body fluid at different stages of life.
a: Edema (swelling) of the ankles and feet

items.q: Body fluids include fluids that are excreted or secreted from the body.
The plasma membrane separates the interstitial fluid from the plasma.
items.e: The plasma membrane separates ICF from the interstitial fluid; the blood vessel wall separates the interstitial fluid from plasma.

items.q: Lean tissues have a lower fluid content than fat tissues.
items.e: Lean tissues have a higher fluid content than fat tissues.

items.q: Interstitial fluid represents the largest portion of the extracellular fluid compartment.
Males have more lean tissue and therefore more body fluid.
Plasma proteins diffuse freely through the pores of the blood capillaries together with water.
items.e: The pores allow water and most dissolved substances to diffuse, except protein.

items.q: Hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid out of the capillary, while osmotic pressure pulls fluid back into it.
The movement of fluid from the interstitial fluid back into the capillaries is called filtration.
items.e: It is called reabsorption; filtration is the exit of fluid from the capillary into the interstitial fluid.

items.q: The maximum body fluid is present at the fetal development stage (~95%).
Edema is the term used for a reduced amount of body fluid.
items.e: A reduced body fluid amount is dehydration; edema is the accumulation of fluid in the interstitial compartment.
